threads.title: Why the busiest team is the slowest

spans.text: Your team is booked to 100% and still misses every date. How can more busyness mean less done?

payoff.text: Past a point, every extra percent of load buys a disproportionate amount of waiting.

spans.text: At 90% utilization work waits nine times as long as it takes; at 95%, nineteen times.

why.text: The last few percent of load cost more waiting than all the rest together.

body.question: Load is only half of what makes work wait. What is the other half?

explanation.text: Utilization is half the story; variability in arrivals and work sizes is the other.

spans.text: Slack is capacity held in reserve for the work you cannot predict, not idle time to cut.
Scheduling everyone at full capacity guarantees queues: any surprise has nowhere to go but the wait.

body.front: Kingman's formula: queue time is a product of which three terms?

back.text: A utilization term, a variability term and the mean service time.
